analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) functional cure strategies often require nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) withdrawal, but clinical trial data on outcomes after NA discontinuation are limited. The study addressed the need to evaluate safety and efficacy of NA cessation following finite xalnesiran-based therapies in virologically suppressed CHB participants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Piranga is a Phase 2 platform trial evaluating four xalnesiran regimens with or without an immunomodulator in virologically suppressed CHB participants. The post hoc evaluation included 121 participants who either continued NA or met prespecified stopping criteria and were monitored for NA discontinuation outcomes.
analysis.methods: Participants who met NA stopping criteria discontinued therapy and were restarted if prespecified restarting criteria were met. Monitoring included assessment for virological relapse (VR) and clinical relapse (CR) during follow-up until the end of the study.
analysis.main_results: Among 121 participants, 40 (33%) discontinued NA. 16 (40%) restarted NA, and 24 (60%) remained off NA by the end of the study. Five participants achieved sustained HBsAg loss and undetectable HBV DNA while off NA, all in arms with an immunomodulator. Nineteen (48%) experienced VR, with 3 (8%) developing CR, all resolving without sequelae.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that NA discontinuation after xalnesiran-based therapy can be safely managed with predefined stopping and restarting criteria and close monitoring. Novelty lies in demonstrating sustained HBsAg loss and undetectable HBV DNA in a subset of participants off NA, particularly those receiving immunomodulator-containing regimens.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings cautiously inform strategies for CHB functional cure by identifying safe NA discontinuation protocols and potential predictors of sustained off-treatment virological control. They also highlight the role of immunomodulators in achieving durable HBsAg loss.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The post hoc nature and single-arm design limit causal inference and generalisability. Evidence strength is moderate due to small sample size, lack of a comparator group, and reliance on predefined stopping/restarting criteria without external validation.

analysis.summary_en: This Phase 2 platform trial evaluated nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) discontinuation following finite xalnesiran-based therapies in 121 virologically suppressed chronic hepatitis B (CHB) participants. Among 40 who discontinued NA, 60% remained off therapy by study end, with 5 achieving sustained HBsAg loss and undetectable HBV DNA, all in immunomodulator-containing arms. Virological relapse occurred in 48% and clinical relapse in 8%, all resolving without sequelae. The authors conclude that NA cessation can be safely managed with prespecified criteria and close monitoring, though the post hoc design and small sample size limit generalisability and causal inference.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection persists as a major public health challenge in Hubei Province, central China, despite reductions in childhood transmission through vaccination. The study was needed to identify drivers of rising adult HBV incidence and to inform targeted control strategies in a historically high-prevalence region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A population-based spatiotemporal epidemiological study analyzed hepatitis B surveillance data from Hubei Province between January 2015 and December 2024, covering 631,361 reported cases across 17 prefecture-level divisions.
analysis.methods: Spatial clustering was assessed using Global Moran's I statistics. Urbanization-related spatial drivers were identified via geographically weighted random forest modeling with SHAP value interpretation, and future incidence trends were predicted using Holt-Winters time series forecasting.
analysis.main_results: The geographically weighted random forest model identified urbanization rate as the primary spatial driver (SHAP value ≈2.0), followed by higher education enrollment rate (≈1.0) and passenger traffic volume (≈0.8). The average annual incidence was 106.19 per 100,000 population, showing a U-shaped temporal trend: declining from 111.75 per 100,000 in 2015 to 83.58 in 2020, then rising to 125.86 in 2024. Adults aged 30–50 years consistently accounted for 40–50% of total cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that HBV burden in Hubei Province has concentrated in adults born before the vaccine era, highlighting horizontal transmission risks in this susceptible cohort. The study is novel in linking urbanization metrics to HBV spatial distribution and projecting future trends using time series forecasting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted screening and revaccination for adults aged 30–50, particularly among high-risk individuals, mobile populations, and rural residents, could reduce incidence and alleviate the regional disease burden in Hubei Province.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on surveillance data, which may be subject to underreporting or misclassification, and the modeling approaches, while robust, depend on the quality and completeness of input data. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations and the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This population-based spatiotemporal study analyzed 631,361 hepatitis B cases reported in Hubei Province, China, from 2015 to 2024 to identify drivers of rising adult incidence and inform control strategies. Using Global Moran's I statistics, geographically weighted random forest modeling, and Holt-Winters forecasting, the study found urbanization rate as the primary spatial driver of HBV distribution (SHAP value ≈2.0), with higher education enrollment and passenger traffic also contributing. The average annual incidence was 106.19 per 100,000, exhibiting a U-shaped trend from 111.75 in 2015 to 83.58 in 2020, then rising to 125.86 in 2024. Adults aged 30–50 consistently accounted for 40–50% of cases, indicating horizontal transmission risks in the pre-vaccine era cohort. The authors conclude that urbanization significantly impacts HBV spatial distribution, with high-risk areas concentrated in the Wuhan metropolitan region, and recommend targeted screening and revaccination for adults aged 30–50, particularly high-risk and mobile populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Low-level residual viremia persists in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs), yet its clinical significance and association with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain insufficiently characterized due to the limited sensitivity of conventional HBV DNA assays.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective case-control study enrolled 208 NUC-treated CHB patients, including 104 with HBV-related HCC matched 1:1 to non-HCC controls, and analyzed serum samples collected up to two years before HCC diagnosis.
analysis.methods: Residual viremia was quantified using a validated droplet digital PCR assay with a lower limit of detection of 1.6 IU/mL, and associations with HCC occurrence, tumor characteristics, and outcomes were assessed using logistic and Cox regression models.
analysis.main_results: Residual viremia within two years was detected in 82.7% of HCC patients versus 49.0% of controls (p < 0.001), and was independently associated with HCC occurrence (OR 7.243, 95% CI 1.862–28.170, p = 0.004), microvascular invasion (44.4% vs. 9.1%, p = 0.033), lower odds of early-stage HCC (OR 0.281, 95% CI 0.094–0.838, p = 0.023), and increased liver-related mortality (HR 4.472, 95% CI 1.212–16.504, p = 0.025).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that high-sensitivity detection of residual viremia in NUC-treated CHB patients identifies those at higher risk for HCC development, more advanced tumor stages, and poorer survival, highlighting the clinical utility of droplet digital PCR for monitoring.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the use of high-sensitivity HBV DNA assays in routine monitoring of NUC-treated CHB patients to stratify HCC risk and guide clinical decision-making.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The retrospective design, single-center setting, and reliance on stored samples limit causal inference and generalizability, and the evidence is derived solely from the abstract, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether low-level residual hepatitis B virus (HBV) viremia in nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC)-treated chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients is associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development and outcomes. Using a validated droplet digital PCR assay with a detection limit of 1.6 IU/mL, residual viremia was measured in serum samples collected up to two years before HCC diagnosis in 104 HBV-related HCC patients and 104 matched non-HCC controls. Residual viremia was detected in 82.7% of HCC patients versus 49.0% of controls (p < 0.001) and was independently associated with HCC occurrence (OR 7.243), microvascular invasion, lower odds of early-stage HCC, and increased liver-related mortality (HR 4.472). The authors conclude that high-sensitivity HBV DNA monitoring may improve risk stratification and clinical outcomes in NUC-treated CHB patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Occult hepatitis B virus (OBI) infection is associated with progressive liver diseases, but the mechanistic basis for this link remains unclear, prompting the study to investigate how OBI drives liver fibrosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A comparative study was conducted involving 40 OBI blood donors and 100 healthy blood donors to assess liver fibrosis using serum biomarkers, the FIB-4 index, and liver stiffness measurement.
analysis.methods: Transcriptome sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells identified IL-17F as upregulated in the OBI group, and mechanistic experiments showed that IL-17F was secreted by CD4+ T cells upon HBcAg stimulation, promoting fibrosis-related cytokines and markers.
analysis.main_results: IL-17F was chiefly secreted by CD4+ T cells upon HBcAg stimulation and functionally promoted the expression of key fibrosis-related cytokines and markers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study reveals a novel pathway wherein HBcAg induces CD4+ T cells to secrete IL-17F, which accelerates liver fibrogenesis, providing a mechanistic basis for OBI-associated liver disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This discovery elucidates a key molecular pathway underlying OBI-related liver disease progression and provides a theoretical foundation for developing IL-17F-targeted diagnostic and anti-fibrotic therapeutic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report study limitations, confounding factors, sample size justification, or statistical uncertainty, limiting confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the mechanistic basis for occult hepatitis B virus (OBI) infection driving liver fibrosis. Using a comparative design with 40 OBI blood donors and 100 healthy controls, the authors assessed liver fibrosis markers and performed transcriptome sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells. They identified IL-17F as significantly upregulated in OBI donors and demonstrated that IL-17F, secreted by CD4+ T cells upon HBcAg stimulation, promotes fibrosis-related cytokines and markers. The findings reveal a novel pathway where HBcAg-induced IL-17F accelerates liver fibrogenesis, offering a mechanistic explanation for OBI-associated liver disease and suggesting potential IL-17F-targeted diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but the long-term risk after hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance is uncertain. The study addressed whether HBsAg seroclearance reduces HCC incidence and identified patient subgroups where surveillance may be unnecessary.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This territory-wide cohort study in Hong Kong identified all adults with CHB who achieved HBsAg seroclearance between 2000 and 2022 using a territory-wide database. The cohort included 13,379 patients with a mean age of 59.7±13.7 years, 59.8% males, and 14.6% with cirrhosis.
analysis.methods: Patients with CHB who cleared HBsAg were identified from a territory-wide database in Hong Kong. Age- and sex-specific population statistics were retrieved from the Hong Kong Cancer Registry and Census and Statistics Department to estimate annual HCC incidence.
analysis.main_results: Among 13,379 patients with HBsAg seroclearance, 274 (2.0%) developed HCC at a median of 5.6 years (IQR 3.1–9.8). Annual HCC incidence was 0.43% (95% CI 0.22%–0.73%) and 0.62% (95% CI 0.50%–0.76%) in patients with cirrhosis aged <50 and ≥50 years, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that patients who cleared HBsAg at younger ages, particularly men under 40 and women under 50 without cirrhosis or additional risk factors, had very low HCC risk. This suggests that routine HCC surveillance may not be necessary in these subgroups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support risk-stratified HCC surveillance strategies in patients with CHB who achieve HBsAg seroclearance, potentially reducing unnecessary medical burden and costs while maintaining safety.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, reliance on a territory-wide database, and lack of detailed data on additional risk factors such as alcohol use or metabolic syndrome. The evidence strength is moderate due to potential unmeasured confounding and generalizability limited to the Hong Kong population.

analysis.summary_en: This territory-wide cohort study in Hong Kong evaluated the long-term incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance in 13,379 adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Over a median follow-up of 5.6 years, 2.0% developed HCC, with annual incidences varying by age, sex, and cirrhosis status. Patients who cleared HBsAg at younger ages, particularly men under 40 and women under 50 without cirrhosis, had very low HCC risk comparable to the general population. The study suggests that routine HCC surveillance may not be necessary in these low-risk subgroups, supporting risk-stratified surveillance strategies. However, limitations include the retrospective design, reliance on a territory-wide database, and potential unmeasured confounding, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B and D virus coinfection represents the most severe form of viral hepatitis, and effective therapies remain limited. The study aimed to assess the safety and efficacy of libevitug, a novel human monoclonal antibody targeting the PreS1 domain of the HBV large envelope protein, in this patient population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a single-center, open-label, phase IIa clinical trial conducted in China that enrolled 9 participants with chronic HBV and HDV coinfection. Participants received intravenous infusion of 20 mg/kg libevitug every 2 weeks for 24 weeks, followed by a 24-week follow-up period.
analysis.methods: The trial administered libevitug at a dose of 20 mg/kg intravenously every 2 weeks for 24 weeks with a subsequent 24-week follow-up. Safety was monitored throughout the study period, and virological and biochemical responses were assessed at predefined intervals.
analysis.main_results: At week 24, 8 participants (88.9%) showed a reduction in HDV RNA of at least 1 log10 from baseline, with 4 (44.4%) achieving undetectable levels. Seven participants (77.8%) achieved a virological response, defined as undetectable HDV RNA or a ≥2 log10 decline from baseline. Among those with elevated baseline ALT, 3 of 5 (60.0%) achieved combined virological and biochemical response. At week 48, 6 participants (66.7%) maintained virological response, with 3 (33.3%) maintaining undetectable HDV RNA. Serum HBsAg levels remained unchanged, and among 7 participants with quantifiable HBV DNA at baseline, 2 (28.6%) achieved undetectable HBV DNA or ≥1 log10 reduction at week 24.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted libevitug as demonstrating promising antiviral activity with substantial HDV RNA reduction, a high rate of ALT normalization, and favorable safety and tolerability in this small cohort. The novelty lies in the first-in-human evaluation of libevitug targeting the PreS1 domain for HBV/HDV coinfection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings cautiously suggest potential for libevitug as an adjunctive therapy in chronic HBV/HDV coinfection, particularly for HDV suppression and ALT normalization, warranting further investigation in larger, controlled trials.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=9), single-center design, and open-label structure limit generalizability and introduce potential bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of a control group and short follow-up period.

analysis.summary_en: This single-center, open-label phase IIa trial evaluated libevitug, a novel anti-HBV monoclonal antibody targeting the PreS1 domain, in 9 patients with chronic HBV and HDV coinfection. Over 24 weeks of treatment with 20 mg/kg libevitug every 2 weeks, 88.9% of participants achieved at least a 1 log10 reduction in HDV RNA, with 44.4% achieving undetectable levels. Virological response (≥2 log10 decline or undetectable HDV RNA) was observed in 77.8%, and 60.0% of those with elevated baseline ALT achieved combined virological and biochemical response. At week 48, 66.7% maintained virological response, though only 33.3% retained undetectable HDV RNA. HBV DNA suppression occurred in 28.6% of those with quantifiable baseline levels, while HBsAg remained unchanged. Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 88.9%, but only 11.1% were treatment-related, with no grade 3 or serious events and no discontinuations. The authors conclude libevitug shows promising antiviral activity and favorable safety, though the small sample and uncontrolled design limit definitive conclusions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) imposes adverse health outcomes and psychosocial challenges, but the impact of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) such as quality of life (QOL) and self-stigma remains poorly understood despite its association with improved clinical outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multi-site study was conducted across six Canadian hepatology clinics, enrolling adults with documented HBsAg clearance to assess PROMs following HBsAg loss.
analysis.methods: Two surveys were administered: one measuring hepatitis B self-stigma and another assessing hepatitis B–related quality of life (HBQOL), with participants drawn from clinics where HBsAg clearance had been documented.
analysis.main_results: Among 84 participants (median age: 60 years), nearly three quarters (72.6%) reported never experiencing self-stigma, and HBQOL scores improved significantly across all six domains (p < 0.001 for each), with the largest relative gains in psychological well-being (60% reduction), transmission concerns (55%), and stigma (53%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that HBsAg loss is associated with substantial improvements in patient-reported stigma and quality of life, highlighting a novel focus on PROMs in hepatitis B clinical care.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that incorporating PROMs into hepatitis B clinical care could better capture treatment experiences and patient well-being, informing patient-centered care strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on abstract-only evidence, lack of a control group, and potential selection bias due to clinic-based recruitment, warranting cautious interpretation of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This multi-site Canadian study assessed patient-reported outcomes following hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss in adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Among 84 participants, 72.6% reported never experiencing self-stigma, and significant improvements were observed in all six domains of hepatitis B–related quality of life (HBQOL), particularly in psychological well-being (60% reduction), transmission concerns (55%), and stigma (53%). The authors conclude that HBsAg loss is associated with meaningful gains in patient-reported stigma and quality of life, emphasizing the importance of integrating PROMs into hepatitis B clinical care. However, the evidence is limited to abstract-level data, lacks a control group, and may be subject to selection bias, reducing the strength of the conclusions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Occult hepatitis B virus infection (OBI) poses a diagnostic and clinical challenge, particularly in cancer patients at risk of viral reactivation during immunosuppressive therapy. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and describe the serological profile of OBI among newly diagnosed cancer patients in India, where limited data are available.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2023, including 100 newly diagnosed cancer patients prior to chemotherapy or radiotherapy at a tertiary care hospital.
analysis.methods: Serum samples negative for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were screened for HBV DNA using quantitative real-time PCR, and serological testing for IgM anti-HBc, Total anti-HBc and anti-HBs antibodies was performed on OBI-positive cases. Demographic and clinical variables were analyzed descriptively.
analysis.main_results: OBI was detected in 7% (7/100) of patients, with HBV DNA levels ranging from 79 to 64,533 IU/mL (mean: 10,823 IU/mL). Among OBI-positive individuals, 42.8% were seropositive (anti-HBc and/or anti-HBs positive) and 57.1% were seronegative.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study observed a 7% prevalence of OBI among treatment-naïve cancer patients, with notably high HBV DNA levels compared to existing data. The presence of OBI in both vaccinated and seronegative individuals highlights the inadequacy of serology-based screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that incorporating HBV DNA testing into routine pre-chemotherapy and radiation therapy screening is strongly recommended to prevent reactivation and improve safety in cancer management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and small sample size, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and serological profile of occult hepatitis B virus infection (OBI) among newly diagnosed cancer patients in India. A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2023, including 100 patients prior to chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Serum samples negative for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were screened for HBV DNA using quantitative real-time PCR, and serological testing was performed on OBI-positive cases. OBI was detected in 7% of patients, with HBV DNA levels ranging from 79 to 64,533 IU/mL. Among OBI-positive individuals, 42.8% were seropositive and 57.1% were seronegative. The study observed a 7% prevalence of OBI, with notably high HBV DNA levels compared to existing data. The presence of OBI in both vaccinated and seronegative individuals highlights the inadequacy of serology-based screening. The findings suggest that incorporating HBV DNA testing into routine pre-chemotherapy and radiation therapy screening is strongly recommended to prevent reactivation and improve safety in cancer management. The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and small sample size, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B persists as a global public health burden with low awareness, underdiagnosis, limited care access, and stigma, and storytelling has been proposed as a communication strategy to address these gaps. The study aimed to evaluate the Hepatitis B Foundation’s International Storytelling Program and its effects on storytellers’ empowerment, confidence, stigma experiences, and advocacy engagement.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted among adults who recorded personal hepatitis B stories through the program, including participants from 22 countries. Quantitative data were collected via an immediate post-recording survey and a follow-up survey 3–6 months later, while qualitative interviews were conducted with 15 participants.
analysis.methods: Survey instruments were developed by the study team and were not previously validated, and descriptive statistics were calculated for quantitative data. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with double coding to ensure consistency, and findings were integrated across methods.
analysis.main_results: Participants reported high satisfaction and immediate benefits, including increased confidence (92%) and perceived preparedness to advocate (96%). At follow-up, 73% reported increased comfort discussing hepatitis B and personal growth, though these findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the small sample size.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the program as a practical, promising approach for empowering individuals affected by hepatitis B and promoting advocacy and stigma reduction globally. The novelty lies in combining quantitative and qualitative evidence to assess storytelling’s multi-dimensional impact on affected individuals.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Storytelling may serve as a complementary strategy to traditional public health approaches for hepatitis B, potentially enhancing empowerment, advocacy, and stigma reduction efforts. The findings suggest value in integrating narrative-based interventions into broader health communication and stigma-reduction initiatives.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Results should be interpreted cautiously due to the small sample size and potential selection bias, and the lack of validated survey instruments may limit measurement reliability. The evidence is assessed as moderate given the mixed-methods design but constrained by methodological limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the Hepatitis B Foundation’s International Storytelling Program using a mixed-methods approach involving adults from 22 countries who recorded personal hepatitis B stories. Quantitative surveys at baseline and 3–6 months later showed high immediate satisfaction, with 92% reporting increased confidence and 96% feeling prepared to advocate, while 73% reported sustained comfort discussing hepatitis B and personal growth at follow-up. Qualitative interviews with 15 participants highlighted emotional processing, identity reframing, and increased willingness to disclose, alongside perceived community awareness gains. The authors conclude the program is a promising strategy for empowerment, advocacy, and stigma reduction, though findings must be interpreted cautiously due to a small sample size, potential selection bias, and unvalidated survey tools. The evidence suggests storytelling could complement traditional public health approaches, warranting further investigation with rigorous methods.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B leads to liver fibrosis, and accurate staging is critical for management, but current non-invasive methods have limitations. The study aimed to assess whether texture analysis of non-contrast MRI sequences could improve diagnostic performance for staging liver fibrosis in these patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study evaluated non-contrast MRI examinations from 66 patients with chronic hepatitis B, categorizing fibrosis as early (F0-F2) or significant (F3-F6). The study was conducted at a single center using routine MRI sequences.
analysis.methods: Histogram-based texture features were extracted from liver parenchyma regions of interest across five MRI sequences. The most informative features were selected using the mRMR algorithm, and multivariable logistic regression models were built for each sequence. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using ROC analysis with AUC, and generalizability was tested via 10-fold cross-validation.
analysis.main_results: The out-of-phase T1-weighted (OP-T1W) sequence achieved the highest AUC of 0.789 (95% CI: 0.677–0.900, p<0.001) for discriminating fibrosis stages, followed by in-phase T1-weighted (AUC=0.723). Other sequences showed lower AUCs (0.657–0.686). No significant differences were found between sequence models (all p>0.05). The OP-T1W sequence had the highest diagnostic accuracy (72.31%) and sensitivity (79.17%), while fat-suppressed T1-weighted had the highest specificity (83.72%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that texture analysis of routine non-contrast MRI sequences provides quantitative, noninvasive information for liver fibrosis staging in chronic hepatitis B, potentially serving as a complementary tool. The novelty lies in demonstrating that OP-T1W texture features can achieve clinically acceptable discrimination without contrast agents.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest texture analysis could enhance noninvasive fibrosis assessment in chronic hepatitis B, reducing reliance on invasive biopsy. However, validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is required before clinical adoption.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-center design, retrospective nature, and small sample size (n=66) limit generalizability and robustness. The evidence strength is moderate due to these constraints and the lack of external validation.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective single-center study evaluated texture analysis of non-contrast MRI sequences for staging liver fibrosis in 66 patients with chronic hepatitis B. Histogram-based texture features were extracted from five MRI sequences and analyzed using logistic regression models with ROC curves and 10-fold cross-validation. The out-of-phase T1-weighted sequence achieved the highest diagnostic performance (AUC=0.789), with acceptable accuracy (72.31%) and sensitivity (79.17%), while fat-suppressed T1-weighted showed the highest specificity (83.72%). No significant differences were found between sequences. The authors conclude that texture analysis may provide noninvasive, quantitative support for fibrosis staging, but further validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is needed due to study limitations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify prognostic factors and establish a nomogram for predicting overall survival in hepatitis B surface antigen-positive cervical cancer patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis of 149 HBsAg-positive cervical cancer patients treated at Yunnan Cancer Hospital between 2015 and 2017 was performed.
analysis.methods: Cox regression identified independent prognostic factors for nomogram development, and internal validation was conducted using the bootstrap resampling method.
analysis.main_results: The nomogram’s predictive accuracy and discriminative capability were evaluated through Harrell’s concordance index, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis, and its performance was compared to the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics staging system.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The nomogram showed superior performance in decision curve analysis and a higher area under the curve compared to the FIGO staging system.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The nomogram can potentially improve prognostic evaluation and treatment planning for HBsAg-positive cervical cancer patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the need for further validation prior to clinical application.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify prognostic factors and establish a nomogram for predicting overall survival in hepatitis B surface antigen-positive (HBsAg-positive) cervical cancer (CC) patients. A retrospective analysis of 149 HBsAg-positive CC patients treated at Yunnan Cancer Hospital between 2015 and 2017 was performed. Cox regression identified independent prognostic factors for nomogram development, and internal validation was conducted using the bootstrap resampling method. The nomogram’s predictive accuracy and discriminative capability were evaluated through Harrell’s concordance index, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis, and its performance was compared to the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) staging system. The nomogram showed superior performance in decision curve analysis and a higher area under the curve compared to the FIGO staging system. The study is limited by its retrospective design and the need for further validation prior to clinical application.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related death in Hong Kong, with chronic hepatitis B infection and/or liver cirrhosis as common risk factors. Routine surveillance using ultrasound plus alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is recommended, but access to ultrasound is limited for many patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study compared the cost-utility of HCC surveillance using 'PIVKA-II + AFP' to the standard-of-care 'US + AFP' in Hong Kong. A health economic model using a Markov-microsimulation framework was adapted using published local data and settings.
analysis.methods: A Markov-microsimulation model was used to compare diagnostic outcomes, overall costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and cost-utility of 'PIVKA-II + AFP' versus 'US + AFP' surveillance. The model was adapted using published local data and settings.
analysis.main_results: Surveillance using 'PIVKA-II + AFP' improved early-stage HCC detection by 4.6 percentage points, reduced false positives by 7.2%, and was associated with a gain of 0.019 QALYs and cost savings of HK $4,144 per individual. Results were particularly favorable for non-cirrhotic chronic hepatitis B patients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that 'PIVKA-II + AFP' surveillance could improve early-stage detection, facilitate timely intervention, and enhance survival and quality of life. The novelty lies in demonstrating cost-effectiveness and diagnostic advantages over standard ultrasound-based surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that 'PIVKA-II + AFP' could serve as a feasible alternative for HCC surveillance in patients with limited access to ultrasound, particularly non-cirrhotic chronic hepatitis B patients. This could inform local health policy and resource allocation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on a modeled economic evaluation using published data, which may not fully capture real-world variability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of prospective clinical validation and potential biases in model assumptions.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the cost-utility of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance using 'PIVKA-II + AFP' compared to the standard 'US + AFP' in Hong Kong. Using a Markov-microsimulation model adapted to local data, the alternative strategy improved early-stage detection by 4.6%, reduced false positives by 7.2%, and achieved a gain of 0.019 QALYs with cost savings of HK $4,144 per individual. The approach was particularly favorable for non-cirrhotic chronic hepatitis B patients. The authors conclude that 'PIVKA-II + AFP' surveillance could be a feasible option for patients with limited access to ultrasound, potentially improving survival and quality of life. However, the evidence is based on a modeled analysis and requires prospective validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the limited human biopsy evidence on whether YAP1-activated hepatocytes, implicated in liver injury and repair, are cleared by Kupffer cells in vivo. It aimed to explore the presence and significance of macrophage-associated YAP1-positive material in early human acute liver injury.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a retrospective exploratory biopsy series of seven adults who underwent clinically indicated liver biopsy within 10 days of presentation or referral for acute liver injury. Biopsies were performed at a median of 5 days after initial presentation.
analysis.methods: Liver biopsy sections were analyzed using hematoxylin and eosin staining, periodic acid-Schiff-diastase staining, YAP1 immunohistochemistry, and double immunofluorescence for YAP1 and CD68. Macrophage-associated YAP1-positive structures were defined as YAP1-positive signals within or adjacent to CD68-positive macrophages in portal or periportal areas.
analysis.main_results: The median age was 52 years, with etiologies including autoimmune hepatitis, overlap syndromes, drug-induced liver injury, acute hepatitis B, and idiopathic acute liver injury. A median of nine portal tracts and five macrophage-associated YAP1-positive structures were evaluated per biopsy, yielding a median YAP1/CD68-positive portal-tract index of 58.3%. ALT normalized after a median of 26 days, and the index showed a nominal inverse association with days to ALT normalization (Spearman rho = -0.86, p = 0.014. Pearson r = -0.79, p = 0.034).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence of YAP1-positive material in spatial association with macrophages in early human acute liver injury, suggesting a potential role in tissue repair or clearance mechanisms. They emphasize that this is a hypothesis-generating observation and not proof of macrophage-mediated phagocytosis or a validated prognostic marker.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that macrophage-associated YAP1-positive material may serve as a biomarker for liver injury severity or recovery potential, warranting further investigation in larger, etiology-specific studies with standardized methodologies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its very small sample size, retrospective design, and lack of standardized biopsy timing or lineage markers, which constrain generalizability and statistical robustness. The evidence strength is low due to the exploratory nature and unstable significance in leave-one-out analyses.

analysis.summary_en: This exploratory biopsy series investigated whether YAP1-activated hepatocytes are cleared by Kupffer cells in early human acute liver injury. Seven adults underwent liver biopsy within 10 days of presentation, with sections analyzed using YAP1 immunohistochemistry and CD68 immunofluorescence to identify macrophage-associated YAP1-positive structures. A median YAP1/CD68-positive portal-tract index of 58.3% was observed, with a nominal inverse association between this index and time to ALT normalization (Spearman rho = -0.86, p = 0.014). The study concludes that YAP1-positive material is spatially associated with macrophages but does not prove phagocytosis or prognostic utility. Limitations include a very small sample size, retrospective design, and unstable statistical significance, warranting larger, standardized studies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B remains a public health problem due to the risk of vertical transmission from pregnant women to the fetus, necessitating early detection. The study aimed to describe HBsAg examination results in second-trimester pregnant women to assess hepatitis B detection in Banyumas.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive observational cross-sectional study was conducted among second-trimester pregnant women. The population included 23 respondents meeting inclusion and exclusion criteria, with venous blood samples collected for HBsAg testing.
analysis.methods: Venous blood samples were analyzed using the HBsAg immunochromatography method (strip test). Data were descriptively analyzed qualitatively to summarize HBsAg examination results.
analysis.main_results: All 23 respondents had negative HBsAg test results, indicating no active hepatitis B virus infection was detected in the sample.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The absence of positive HBsAg results suggests low hepatitis B prevalence in this population during the second trimester. The study highlights the utility of strip tests as an initial screening method for early detection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of HBsAg strip tests for routine screening in pregnant women to prevent mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=23) and single-center design limit generalizability, and the cross-sectional approach precludes causal inference. The evidence is low due to methodological constraints and lack of statistical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined HBsAg prevalence in 23 second-trimester pregnant women in Banyumas using immunochromatography strip tests. All participants tested negative for HBsAg, indicating no active hepatitis B infections in the sample. The authors conclude that strip tests are suitable for initial screening to prevent mother-to-child transmission. However, the small sample size, single-center design, and qualitative analysis limit the generalizability and robustness of the findings. The evidence is considered low due to methodological constraints and lack of statistical validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Methylophiopogonone A (MON-A) is an anti-inflammatory constituent of Ophiopogon japonicus with reported therapeutic potential for liver fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B and SARS-CoV-2 infection, but its metabolic fate and safety profile were not well understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the metabolic profile of MON-A using liver microsomes and cryopreserved hepatocytes from humans and three preclinical species (rat, dog, and monkey) with ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole/Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Orbitrap-HRMS).
analysis.methods: MON-A was incubated with each system and analyzed in positive electrospray ionization mode, with data processed using Compound Discoverer software and metabolite structures characterized based on accurate mass and MS2 fragment ions.
analysis.main_results: A total of 14 metabolites were identified, with primary metabolic pathways including hydroxylation, oxidative methylenedioxyphenyl (MDP) ring-opening, oxidation, and glucuronidation, and M11 (a glucuronide conjugate) being the most abundant metabolite across all species.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study clarifies the metabolic fate of MON-A, revealing its biotransformation pathways and identifying the formation of reactive metabolites, including four glutathione conjugates and quinone methide species, which highlights potential safety considerations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings establish a foundation for evaluating the therapeutic efficacy and safety profile of MON-A during preclinical development, particularly regarding its metabolic activation and potential reactive metabolite formation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report sample sizes, quantitative metabolite abundances, or statistical analyses, limiting the strength of conclusions about the relative importance of pathways or species differences.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized the metabolic profile of methylophiopogonone A (MON-A), an anti-inflammatory compound with potential therapeutic applications in liver fibrosis and viral infections. Using liver microsomes and hepatocytes from humans and preclinical species, the authors identified 14 metabolites via UHPLC-Orbitrap-HRMS, with glucuronidation, hydroxylation, and oxidation as key pathways. M11, a glucuronide conjugate, was the most abundant metabolite across species. Reactive metabolite formation was indicated by four glutathione conjugates and quinone methide species, suggesting metabolic activation via the C2-C3 double bond in the A-ring. The work provides foundational insights into MON-A's biotransformation and safety, supporting its preclinical evaluation, though the abstract lacks quantitative details and statistical context.

analysis.brief_en: Aligos Therapeutics announced the global completion of enrollment in its Phase 2 B-SUPREME study of pevifoscorvir sodium for chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. The trial enrolled 245 adults split between HBeAg-positive (131) and HBeAg-negative (114) groups across international sites. The randomized, double-blind study compares pevifoscorvir sodium monotherapy to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate over 48 weeks, with primary endpoints assessing HBV DNA suppression. Topline safety and efficacy data are anticipated in late Q3 2027. The investigational oral capsid assembly modulator has shown promising antiviral activity in earlier trials.

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-15. Event date: 2025 (coverage year). WHO-UNICEF WUENIC report released on 2026-07-15.
analysis.location_and_population: Target population: newborns within 24 hours of birth.
analysis.event: WHO and UNICEF questioned India’s official estimate of hepatitis B birth-dose coverage (HEPBB) for 2025, stating the reported 92% coverage overstates actual performance. The agencies estimate actual national HEPBB coverage at 70%, indicating 30% of newborns missed the vaccine within the recommended window. The discrepancy is flagged in the WHO-UNICEF Estimates of National Immunisation Coverage (WUENIC) report.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: India reported 92% HEPBB coverage in 2025. WHO-UNICEF estimate: 70% (30% missed). Hepatitis B transmission risk from mother to infant persists without timely birth-dose vaccination. Chronic infection risk in infants: up to 90%. India’s routine childhood immunisation remains high: DTP1 (97%), measles (98%), rubella (98%), pneumococcal (97%), DTP3 (95%), hepatitis B3 (95%), IPV (95%), BCG (91%), rotavirus (91%). Globally, 13.5 million children remained zero-dose in 2025.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO and UNICEF flagged the HEPBB coverage discrepancy as ‘Estimate challenged by: R-’ due to concerns over reported coverage denominator and target population. Agencies await final results from India’s National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) for review. Indian government has not yet publicly responded to the challenge. Routine immunisation programme continues high coverage across most vaccines.

analysis.brief_en: On 15 July 2026, WHO and UNICEF released the WUENIC report questioning India’s reported 92% coverage of the hepatitis B birth-dose vaccine for 2025, estimating actual national coverage at only 70%. The agencies flagged the discrepancy as inconsistent with their final estimate due to concerns over the reported denominator and target population. Hepatitis B birth-dose vaccination within 24 hours of birth is critical to prevent mother-to-child transmission, which can lead to chronic infection in up to 90% of infected infants. Despite the challenge, India’s routine childhood immunisation remains strong, with high coverage across most vaccines, including DTP1 (97%) and measles (98%). The government has not yet responded to the agencies’ assessment.

analysis.location_and_population: Research conducted at Chongqing Medical University, China. validated in HBV transgenic mice and pAAV/HBV1.2 mouse models. Human liver samples from patients with chronic HBV infection were analyzed.
analysis.event: A mechanistic study published in Genes & Diseases identified a ROS-dependent signaling cascade that activates the Jak2/Stat3 pathway, triggering hepatic inflammatory responses in chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. The event is reported as a scientific finding, not an outbreak or public-health incident.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: No cases, deaths, or exposures were reported. The study describes molecular mechanisms underlying HBV-induced liver inflammation and identifies ROS-dependent Jak2/Stat3 activation as a potential therapeutic target.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study is preliminary and mechanistic, based on transcriptomic analyses, cell-line experiments, and mouse models. Further validation in clinical settings and human trials is required. The source is a reputable scientific news outlet summarizing peer-reviewed research.

analysis.brief_en: A study published on 17 July 2026 by researchers at Chongqing Medical University reveals a molecular mechanism linking chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to liver inflammation. The team found that HBV replication disrupts mitochondrial function, causing excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation that activates the Jak2/Stat3 inflammatory pathway via Nrf2-regulated cytokines IL-6 and IL-8. Experiments in HBV transgenic mice and patient liver samples confirmed this ROS-dependent cascade, while antioxidant treatment (NAC) reduced inflammation. The findings identify ROS-driven Jak2/Stat3 signaling as a potential therapeutic target to prevent inflammation-driven liver disease progression in chronic HBV patients.

analysis.time: The event occurred on 12 September 2025, with the coroner's report published on 10 July 2026 and the response sent on 6 July 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The event took place in Inner London North, UK, involving a 41-year-old patient with a renal transplant and chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.event: A coroner raised concerns over the lack of national guidance on prescribing and monitoring for hepatitis B reactivation, following the death of a patient who died from complications due to the inadvertent discontinuation of necessary medical treatment.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The patient died from complications of hepatitis B reactivation. The coroner noted a lack of national guidance and specialized commissioning for hepatitis B services, which could pose a risk to other patients.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The coroner directed concerns to the British Viral Hepatitis Group and the UK Health Security Agency. The British Association for the Study of the Liver (BASL) responded that it does not lead the development of clinical guidelines, and that monitoring and prescribing responsibilities vary between NHS trusts.

The coroner's report, published on 10 July 2026, highlighted that the patient's medication was discontinued in early 2025, leading to hepatitis B reactivation. The British Association for the Study of the Liver (BASL) responded that it does not lead the development of clinical guidelines and that responsibilities vary between NHS trusts.

Caplan, PhD) publicly criticized a proposed unethical study in Guinea-Bissau that would test hepatitis B vaccination efficacy using a placebo control in 15,000 children. analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Not reported in the supplied evidence. The commentary does not provide case counts, death counts, or current disease burden data for Guinea-Bissau. The proposed study involved 15,000 children, but no outcomes or risks are detailed.

The ethicist and others advocate for immediate vaccination programs in Guinea-Bissau instead of further study. analysis.brief_en: A New York University medical ethicist has condemned a proposed unethical study in Guinea-Bissau that aimed to test hepatitis B vaccination efficacy using a placebo control in 15,000 children. Arthur L. Caplan, PhD, argued the vaccine is already proven safe and effective, and the study design exploited poverty in one of the world’s poorest nations. The study has been suspended but not definitively canceled, and the ethicist called for immediate vaccination programs instead. The commentary highlights ongoing debates over hepatitis B vaccination policies in the U.S. and globally.

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-14. Event period: January 2018 to December 2025 (retrospective cohort study).
analysis.location_and_population: United States, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Population: 93,163 live births at three University of Pennsylvania health system hospitals. Affected groups: female and male newborns.
analysis.event: A retrospective cohort study published in JAMA Network Open reported that female newborns were more than twice as likely as male newborns to have parents decline intramuscular vitamin K (VK) prophylaxis at birth, and modestly more likely to miss the hepatitis B vaccine (HBV) birth dose. The study was conducted by researchers from the University of Pennsylvania and published in JAMA Network Open.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among 93,163 live births, 777 infants (8.3 per 1,000 births) did not receive VK prophylaxis, and 9,400 (100.9 per 1,000 births) did not receive the HBV birth dose. Female newborns had an adjusted odds ratio (aOR) of 2.03 for VK nonreceipt and 1.06 for HBV nonreceipt compared with male newborns. By 2025, VK decline rates rose to 19.8 per 1,000 female births and 10.1 per 1,000 male births. HBV decline rates reached 173.7 per 1,000 female births and 166.3 per 1,000 male births. The study notes that infants without VK prophylaxis face increased bleeding risk, and hospitals often do not perform circumcision without it.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study authors suggest circumcision incentives may explain the VK disparity, as parents seeking circumcision for sons may accept VK despite hesitancy. No comparable procedural incentive explained the HBV gap. The authors call for additional research to understand disparities and assess outcomes such as VK deficiency bleeding (VKDB) or neonatal hepatitis B infection. They also note the study was limited to a single health system, potentially limiting generalizability.

analysis.brief_en: A retrospective cohort study of 93,163 live births at three Philadelphia hospitals found female newborns were more than twice as likely as males to have parents decline intramuscular vitamin K prophylaxis, and modestly more likely to miss the hepatitis B vaccine birth dose. Among the cohort, 777 infants (8.3 per 1,000) did not receive vitamin K, and 9,400 (100.9 per 1,000) missed the HBV dose. Declines worsened over time, with female newborns showing higher rates by 2025. Researchers suggest circumcision incentives may drive the vitamin K disparity, while the hepatitis B gap remains unexplained. The study, published in JAMA Network Open, coincides with a recent CDC policy shift allowing shared decision-making for HBV birth dose, raising concerns about reduced coverage.
